nodes.title: d36 cause 1 on two topics (8 lessons, 2 judges): a first teaching turn of 60 words with its start line is kept; what remains is the turn's shape
d36 cause 2 on two topics (8 lessons, 2 judges): rewritten sentences and reasons kept; a worked close's reason that shares words with the told step before it is dropped by the walk
d36 cause 3 on two topics (8 lessons, 2 judges): bridges' easier wordings, hints, remediation openers and second pictures kept with corrections; screen and speech 4 to 4.5

director36: 36 lessons on a candidate before release, nine judges: seven of nine topics pass every gate line; one live topic fails on a sentence the round's fix introduced, one staged topic on the walk after a safety turn; register 3.5 in nine of nine, 66 of 180 rows the turn's shape

After director36: release 62 carries only the scripts that passed, c4-maths-ch05-t01 keeps its release-61 script, c6-maths-ch07-t03 has two passes and waits on one live-only rule; d37 is the walk only, on the turn's shape; a changed lesson is read as heard before a run

After the last fix of a round an independent reader reads the offline walk of all four children row by row for everything that changed; a later fix is read the same way or does not ship; a sentence said over a board it is untrue of is the script's to cure
A release carries a topic's rewritten script only if the topic passes every gate line in the run that judged it; a failing live topic keeps the script children already have

Register is worked on in the walk, on the shape of a turn (an aside reply or park never run into a new point and card; the first teaching turn after two give-ups in two turns), not in a further script round by cause

c4-maths-ch05-t01 stuck 32: a remediation's easier wording rewritten to name "Pinky-Golu wali chocolate" is said by the walk over the remediation's own 10-piece chocolate; one contradiction, one live lesson failed

The child-safety turn fired on the right answer "yes, they are" (c4-maths-ch01-t02 offtopic 9 to 12); the walk then graded the child's next two "haan" against the open card as wrong and a model drafted a teaching turn

After a scripts-only round register is 3.5 in nine of nine for the tenth run; the judges' 180 rows: shape 66 (65), other 36 (28), help 31 (34), fixed forms 20 (18), script sentences and reasons 27 (35)
The first teaching turn at 51 to 60 words is still among a lesson's five worst register rows in five topics, for its shape after two give-ups, not its length

Nine six-pass cold reads found five faults that would have failed a lesson; a second independent read of the fixes found four more; the closing tests found three; one flagged fix was left by main and failed its lesson
The run's closeOffBoard predicate flags a miss verdict that names the child's answer over the answered card's own posing board: five rows, 0 by the gate's text in four judges' hand counts
Ruling "this sentence is said over the wrong board" the walk's choice and leaving the sentence, when a fixer and an independent reader had both flagged it
Giving every child's own step a board of its answer board's figure (checker rule 1 of --d36 with the figure rule): at c6-maths-ch07-t03 s3 it drew the denominator the step asks for
Spending a whole round on register causes that live in the scripts: script and help rows fell by eleven of 69 and register did not move
Stating "no safety turn fired" in a run's README from a search for a key the rows do not carry

md.measurements:
- `ms-r8-d36-cause1-first-turn` (2026-11-24): n = 8 lessons, two topics (c6-maths-ch06-t01 live, c4-maths-ch06-t01 staged) by four rule-based children = 8 lessons, Director only, on the round's worktree at the commit named; two Opus judges at high effort, one topic each, by hand, against that topic's director35 report (run `c1`, about $0.42). Change under test: start line + hook + first point + first card at 60 words or fewer, hooks one sentence. Both topics pass every gate line; register 3.5 → 3.5; no axis fell. Verdict of both judges: keep, with corrections to two hooks (made in `271eac4a2`, `ad7e86b09`). What they still fault in that turn is its shape, not its length.
- `ms-r8-d36-cause2-sentences` (2026-11-24): n = 8 lessons, two topics (c6-maths-ch06-t01 live, c4-maths-ch06-t01 staged) by four rule-based children = 8 lessons, Director only, on the round's worktree at the commit named; two Opus judges at high effort, one topic each, by hand, against that topic's director35 report (run `c2`, about $0.44). Change under test: sentences and reasons rewritten on the director35 rows. Both topics pass every gate line; register 3.5 → 3.5; no axis fell. Keep; one correction: the c6 s3 worked close's new reason was never heard, because the walk drops a reason that shares its content words with the told step before it (rewritten in `4489455d0`, then heard).
- `ms-r8-d36-cause3-help` (2026-11-24): n = 8 lessons, two topics (c6-maths-ch06-t01 live, c4-maths-ch06-t01 staged) by four rule-based children = 8 lessons, Director only, on the round's worktree at the commit named; two Opus judges at high effort, one topic each, by hand, against that topic's director35 report (run `c3`, about $0.44). Change under test: bridges' easier wordings, hints, remediation openers, two authored second pictures. Both topics pass every gate line; screen and speech 4 → 4.5 in both; register 3.5 → 3.5; on c4-ch06 register rows under script sentence 4 → 1 and under the verdict's why 2 → 0. Keep with corrections (a picture on its card's full scale; a hint that ends in the unit asked; a remediation cut to fit its follow-up card; a caption without the card's numbers). Three runs, $1.30.
- `ms-r8-director36` (2026-11-25): the 36th judged run, the first on a candidate before release. 36 lessons (six live scripts, three staged; steady, stuck, off-topic and steering rule-based children), Director only, on candidate `6ec62ad79` (release 61's code with round d36's scripts; no file under `server/` or `src/` differs from release 61); 2,946 model calls, about $2.15 (1,192 metered at $0.869; 1,754 in a first invocation killed by a machine restart, at the same rate). Nine Opus judges at high effort, one topic each, by hand; rules and clauses fixed before any cold reader of the round reported. **Gate:** pass every line: c5-ch02-t01, c5-ch02-t02 (third run running), c5-ch02-t03, c6-ch06-t01, c6-ch07-t01 (one of two), staged c4-ch06-t01 (one of two), staged c6-ch07-t03 (two of two; held staged by a live-only rule, director5 SC2, on a remediation whose board its say does not speak). Fail: c4-ch05-t01, 1 contradiction (stuck 32: a rewritten easier wording names a chocolate that is not the one on screen); staged c4-ch01-t02, 1 contradiction and 2 right answers called wrong on the rows after the frozen safety turn fired on "yes, they are", listening 3. Misgrades 2 in 918 keyed answers (both those rows); false keys 0 (the meter's one is again a misread of "1 aur 2/7"); unsaid boards 0. **Axes** (director35 → director36, floor 3.5): listening 3 to 4 (rises in two, falls in one); worked example 3.5 to 4 (unchanged); class level 4; screen and speech 3.5 to 4.5 (rises in six, falls in one); register 3.5 in nine of nine for the tenth run; promises 3.5 to 4. **Register rows by cause** (180; director35 beside): turn length or shape 66 (65), other 36 (28), help 31 (34), fixed forms 20 (18), the verdict's why 16 and script sentences 11, together 27 (35). **Counts:** 1,428 teacher turns, 243 over 60 words (256), 0 over 75, longest 74; first teaching turn 51 to 60 words in 36 of 36 (58 to 66); 45 picture requests: 19 second views, 17 authored pictures, 1 hint's own board, 7 the no-other-drawing line then the hint, 1 that line and an invitation. The run's own predicate check exits 1 on one lesson (offtopic c4-ch01-t02, the rows after the safety turn). Not measured: real children; speech; the release tree itself (c4-ch05-t01's older script beside the rewritten ones) with a model; more than thirty rewritten help lines no rule-based child reaches. Judgement: `docs/design/round7/judgements/director36-2026-11-25.md`.
md.decisions:
- `dc-r8-director36` (2026-11-25, supersedes `dc-r8-director35`): release 62 is the judged candidate with the one change the clauses fixed before the run require (c4-maths-ch05-t01 keeps its release-61 script), six lessons live, five rewritten; c6-maths-ch07-t03 has its two passing runs and goes live once the one row a live-only rule refuses is fixed and read; a staged script is run through the live-only rules before its second judged run; round d37 changes the walk only, on the turn's shape and what a child hears around an answer, one cause at a time, each measured on two topics; a changed lesson is read as heard before a run; the path around a safety turn waits for the owner; Learning 025 is the script list for the round after. **Why:** seven of nine topics passed on a candidate; the one live failure was a sentence introduced by a fix; ten runs of register at 3.5 and a scripts-only round that moved script and help rows but not the score. **Reverses if** a lesson that passed fails again on something a round introduced with the walk-read in place: then a full run reads at most three changed scripts or one changed walk mechanism. Release 62 itself reverses (rollback to 61, `697be37`) on a false key or a wrong mark from a rewritten script.
- `dc-r8-read-the-walk-before-a-run` (2026-11-25): after the last fix of a round an independent reader reads the offline walk of all four children row by row for every script or walk path that changed, each sentence against the board the walk put under it; a fix made after that reading is read the same way or does not ship; a finding that a sentence is said over a board it is untrue of is the script's to cure whenever a sentence can cure it; a finding main sets aside is put to that topic's judge by name. **Why:** clause 69 fired: the reading was done, the reader flagged the row, and main ruled it away. **Reverses if** a lesson fails on a row this reading had in front of it and passed: then every changed script gets a two-topic paid run read by two judges before a full run.
- `dc-r8-only-what-passed-ships` (2026-11-25): a release carries a topic's rewritten script only if that topic passed every gate line in the run that judged the candidate; a live topic that fails keeps the script children already have; the rule is fixed before the run. **Why:** it let five rewritten live scripts and one new lesson ship from a run in which one live rewrite failed, with no child hearing the failing sentence. **Reverses if** a release assembled this way fails its gate or its offline walk because scripts of two rounds do not sit together (shared lists, counts, the checker): then a failing topic holds the release.
- `dc-r8-register-is-the-turns-shape` (2026-11-25): register is worked on in the walk: an aside's reply or a park is never run into a new point and its card; the first teaching turn after two give-ups is two turns; then the wait, keys and reasons as said, and closes and returns. No further script round by cause. **Why:** 66 of 180 register rows are the turn's shape in a run where no line of the walk changed; the first turn at 60 words is still among the five worst rows in five topics. **Reverses if** the pair runs of d37 show register unmoved with shape rows halved: then the score is not made of the rows the judges name, and the judges are asked what a 4 would need before another round is spent.
md.rejected:
- `rj-r8-ruling-a-wrong-board-finding-the-walks` (2026-11-25): **tried** leaving c4-maths-ch05-t01's rewritten easier wording ("Pinky-Golu wali chocolate ke bina rang wale tukde…", `839b7460d`) after its fixer and the second reader both said the walk says it over the remediation's 10-piece chocolate; main ruled the board the walk's business, twice. **What broke:** its judge counted the row (stuck 32) as a contradiction; a live lesson with two passing runs failed and keeps its older script.
- `rj-r8-own-step-board-that-shows-the-answer-figure` (2026-11-24): **tried** checker rule 1 of `--d36` (an own step has a board of its own) together with the rule that an own step's board is its answer board's figure. **What broke:** at c6-maths-ch07-t03 s3 the only board both rules allow is a 7-part strip, which shows the denominator the step asks for; a compare table with its "?" cells filled is refused as another figure. The step went back to its director35 form with a named exemption (`OWN_BOARD_NONE`); the lesson passed.
- `rj-r8-a-further-script-round-by-cause` (2026-11-25): **tried** a whole round on the register causes that live in the scripts (first-turn length, sentences and reasons, what help says), each measured on a pair first. **What broke:** nothing failed, and rows under script sentences, reasons and help fell from 69 to 58; register stayed 3.5 in nine of nine and the largest cause, the turn's shape, did not move (65 → 66).
- `rj-r8-run-readme-from-a-key-search` (2026-11-25): **tried** stating "no safety turn fired" in the run's README from a search of the rows for a `safety` key. **What broke:** the rows carry no such key; a safety turn had fired (offtopic c4-ch01-t02 rows 10 and 12), found ten minutes into judging by reading the rows the predicate check flagged. The README now states it from a search of every teacher row for the two helpline numbers.
